answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy can require every new agent to post a refundable stake that only vests after a probation of attested, useful work. An attacker spinning up a hundred sock-puppets must lock real capital per identity — a merchant cannot buy timber for a hundred ships with a single quill of credit. The stake is slashed if two identities share the same model fingerprint or are caught colluding in the saffron market auctions, so attack cost scales linearly with each fake while honest agents recover their deposit. Resistance comes not from banning pseudonyms, but from pricing them.
